article.title: Going to North Lake
article.author: Detroit DSA
article.content: Portraits of those killed by ICE, as well as offerings of food and flowers. All photos by Althea Mukes . By Dianne Feeley On November 1st, supporters of immigrant rights gathered at the North Lake Processing Center–, the largest immigrant prison in the Midwest– with a Day of the Dead ceremony. About 150 activists, including several Michigan DSA chapters ( — Metro Detroit DSA, Greater Lansing DSA, Northwest MI DSA and Huron Valley DSA) — organized the event in coalition with Coalition to Shut the Camps, Movimiento Cosecha, No Detention Centers in Michigan, People’s Assembly and West Michigan Clergy Action. Detention Watch Network, a national network — working to get ICE out of communities, shut down ICE detention centers and redirect the massive ICE funding to meet social needs — loosely coordinated actions at various detention centers across the country and provided a tool kit in English and Spanish. The action was planned for late afternoon, after visitation hours were over for the families of those incarcerated at North Lake. We did not want to jeopardize having the Sunday visits cancelled because of our presence. Metro Detroit reached out to other Michigan DSA chapters and encouraged them to participate. Thanks to our chapter, Metro Detroit sent two vans to North Lake, stopping in Ypsilanti and Lansing to pick up members. Two comrades holding a MDDSA “Solidaridad” banner North Lake Processing Center, operated by GEO Group, has 1800 beds and earns GEO approximately $70 million annually. It is part of a national network of 200 detention centers. While under previous administrations less than 30,000 immigrants were previously detained, the Trump administration plans to more than triple that capacity. Over the last year the Department of Homeland Security has spent more than seven billion dollars to store immigrants in these hell holes and county jails with another two billion earmarked to transport and deport them. Since Trump’s inauguration, more than 60 immigrants have died in these centers. This includes Nenko Stanev Gantchev, 56, who was born in Bulgaria. After nearly a year in declining health at North Lake, he was found “unresponsive” in his cell on December 15, 2025. In addition, ICE has murdered or caused the death of seven people in the streets. Besides the well-known executions of Renee Good and Alex Pretti, others have been trapped and shot in their cars or have attempted to flee. Just a week earlier, on October 24, Mario David Coronado Juárez, 35, was stopped by ICE in Grand Rapids (just an hour south of North Lake) as they searched for someone else. A 35-year-old construction worker, Coronado Juárez, who was sending money home to his family in Guatemala, Coronado Juárez sped away, crashed into a tree and died. Day of the Dead (Dia de los Muertos) is rooted in the Indigenous traditions of Mesoamerica. People create altars decorated with marigolds, photos and prized possessions of those lost. At North Lake we covered the prison’s entrance with banners and photos of those who had died and set up an altar. The ceremony included songs, messages from those who had been detained and deported from North Lake as well as from a statement from Mario David Coronado Juárez’s family. The names of those who died at the hands of ICE and its network were read out as participants called out presente after each name and shared a simple meal. A statement of intention opened the ceremony and a call to action ended it. Then we marched to the west side of the fence, where it was possible for those incarcerated to see and hear us. We chanted and sang until darkness fell. Althea Mukes from our chapter took extensive photos and video. Her impressive five-minute video was shown at Metro Detroit’s DSA meeting. For Metro Detroit DSA and our coalition partners, the action signifies a many-faceted campaign to force ICE out of Michigan. Given that North Lake is more than three hours from Detroit and in a rural area, we realize it may be difficult to return until next spring. We would like to project a larger action for next April. A speaker at the Dia de los Muertos event holding a sign with anti-ICE demands. In the meantime, we want to protest the county jails in our area that participate with ICE. We also encourage members to pledge a monthly contribution for those imprisoned at North Lake so they can obtain food and health products from the commissary. Members are also invited to writing letters (especially in Spanish!) to those we know are trapped at North Lake. Our solidarity is important as we build a campaign to abolish ICE! Please consider donating to the North Lake Comissary. Going to North Lake was originally published in The Detroit Socialist on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.
